case_name: Jitu @ Jitender v State Of M.P.
respondent:
State Of M.P.
Supreme Court of India

5 March 2009
CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 679 OF 2006
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr.Arijit Pasayat, J.
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, Indore Bench upholding the conviction of the appellant for offence punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'IPC'). Four persons faced trial for allegedly committing murder of one Umesh (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased'). Accused-Mukesh died during the pendency of the trial, while another accused Pappu@Deepak was acquitted by the trial court.
2.  It is stated that on 17.11.1995, the occurrence took place in which due to the assaults made by the accused persons Umesh breathed his last, while three of the persons Bhagirath PW8, Bherulal PW9 and Yogesh PW10 sustained injuries. facts: On 17.11.1995, the occurrence took place in which due to the assaults made by the accused persons Umesh breathed his last, while three of the persons Bhagirath PW8, Bherulal PW9 and Yogesh PW10 sustained injuries.
The accused persons were charged for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 and Section 324 read with Section 34 IPC.
Accused-Mukesh died during the pendency of the trial and accused-Deepak was acquitted of the charges.
The appellant's appeal before the High Court was dismissed.
The stand taken before the High Court is reiterated in the present appeal by the learned counsel for the appellant.

It is to be noted that PW8, the informant on whose evidence trial court and the High Court placed reliance had categorically stated that it was accused Rakesh who had attacked the deceased with a sword,
holding: The conviction of the appellant is altered to one under Section 326 IPC and custodial sentence of seven years is imposed upon him.
